transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ava Thompson (Redwood AE), Diego Rivera (Redwood SE), Mira Patel (NovaPay Head of ML Ops), Samir Khan (NovaPay Platform Eng), Olivia Chen (NovaPay SRE)

Summary:
Quick follow-up from last week's incident where NovaPay saw intermittent 5xx spikes and client timeouts during peak batch replay. Goal: review initial findings, assign next steps for logs/replay, and agree mitigation (retry/backoff, rate-limiting tweaks, circuit breaker).

Topics:
- Incident timeline recap
- Root-cause hypotheses (autoscaler overshoot, tokenization/kv cache cold-starts, misconfigured retries)
- Logs and traces needed for deeper analysis
- Short-term mitigations and longer-term reliability work

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava Thompson: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight — we have about 45 minutes. quick check, mira, are you on?
[00:18] Mira Patel: yup i'm here, thanks. sorry i was pulled into another call earlier so i may jump in with a note.
[00:26] Diego Rivera: hey, diego from redwood se. i dug into the traces overnight and pulled some initial 5xx buckets.
[00:34] Samir Khan: hey all. olivia's here too but she's muted for now.
[00:40] Olivia Chen: hi, unmuted now. so quick context, we replayed the pilot traffic yesterday to try to reproduce the error bursts, and we saw two patterns: short-lived 5xx spikes correlated with autoscaler churn, and longer tail timeouts during long-tail prompts.
[01:02] Diego Rivera: yep that matches what i saw. the 5xx traces are mostly 502/504 from the fronting proxy, but there are also occasional 5xx returned by the inference node when the kv cache is cold and memory pressure rises — or at least that's one hypothesis.
[01:25] Ava Thompson: quick clarification: when you say fronting proxy, is that Nginx in front of the load balancer? or a managed gateway?
[01:32] Samir Khan: it's our NGINX + sidecar envoy setup. we do have aggressive timeouts at the gateway of 10s which i think may be clipping some of the longer gen requests.
[01:44] Mira Patel: and our pilot used a bursty traffic pattern, lots of short tests followed by heavier batch runs. we should've smoothed it, but this is the profile we wanted to capture.
[01:58] Diego Rivera: thanks, that's super helpful. on the redwood side i pulled the request logs and saw a handful of retries from the client that then caused our rate-limiter to throttle a few connections. there may be retry storms exacerbating the autoscaler thrash.
[02:20] Olivia Chen: so the sequence looks like: client retries -> spikes in incoming QPS -> autoscaler scales up new nodes -> new nodes have cold kv caches -> initial requests time out or fail -> client retries again. vicious cycle.
[02:40] Ava Thompson: right, classic cold-start + retry loop. some quick mitigation options: increase gateway timeout temporarily, add jitter to client retry policy, and enable prefix caching on the model to reduce cold-start latency.
[02:59] Samir Khan: increasing the timeout is easy, we can do that tonight. but i'm worried about cost if nodes stay up. can you explain more about prefix caching?
[03:12] Diego Rivera: sure — prefix/KV caching holds recent token keys, so when similar prompts come in the model doesn't rebuild the full KV for every request. in our runtime it's called the KV cache and we've seen up to 40-60% latency reduction for similar prompts. it also reduces memory pressure on new nodes. it's not magic but it helps with the cold tail.
[03:48] Mira Patel: sounds good. is enabling that a config toggle or a model change?
[03:54] Diego Rivera: mostly runtime config and model profile. we can enable it for the pilot models; we may want to run a short test to validate quality isn't affected.
[04:06] Ava Thompson: can we also set a short grace period in autoscaler so new nodes don't immediately receive full load?
[04:12] Diego Rivera: yes, that's another pattern — slow ramp to warm up caches. on redwood dedicated we can tune the routing to favor warmed nodes during scale events. for the private pilot we can provide guidelines for kube-probe / readiness delay.
[04:32] Samir Khan: we run a custom HPA with aggressive scaling (target CPU 40%). maybe we soften that.
[04:38] Olivia Chen: regarding 5xx origin identification, diego, can you share the S3 CSV of trace ids you extracted?
[04:46] Diego Rivera: yep i'll upload the trace list and the nginx logs to the shared drive. note that the transcription of some product names in earlier notes was messed up — 'Redwood Dedicate' shows up — it's actually Redwood Dedicated.
[04:59] Mira Patel: lol noted.
[05:03] Ava Thompson: good catch. ok moving to next, retries — what do you have configured on the client side?
[05:12] Samir Khan: currently three retries with exponential backoff starting at 200ms, no jitter. we added retries to handle transient network flakiness, but looks like it's making it worse.
[05:22] Diego Rivera: add a randomized jitter and cap the retry rate; also consider a small circuit break after N consecutive 5xx to avoid retry storms.
[05:32] Mira Patel: can you sketch an example policy?
[05:35] Diego Rivera: sure — e.g., retries=2, base=300ms, jitter=uniform(0,200ms), circuit-break after 5xx x 5 in 30s window, then backoff 30s. i can put this in a doc.
[05:50] Ava Thompson: diego to produce the recommended retry policy and share as a small markdown in the drive.
[05:56] Olivia Chen: another question — are there rate-limiting rules on the redwood side we should be aware of? we saw 429s in some traces.
[06:04] Diego Rivera: yes, we enforce per-tenant rate limits for the pilot tier. during the incident some of our internal throttles kicked in because of the retry amplification. we can temporarily raise the per-minute cap while we stabilize if you want.
[06:18] Samir Khan: that would help for the short-term. can you quantify the increase and expected cost delta?
[06:24] Ava Thompson: i'll send a quick pricing note — but diego can also run a cost estimate for the 48h replay and the temporary cap increase.
[06:34] Diego Rivera: will do. i'll include approximate token counts and cost impact.
[06:40] Mira Patel: ok on logs — i'll ask samir to pull the autoscaler events and share the HPA config.
[06:46] Samir Khan: yes, will attach to the ticket.
[06:49] Ava Thompson: recap of concrete next steps: diego uploads nginx logs and trace ids, diego runs 48h replay and summarizes, mira + samir share traffic profile and autoscaler config, redwood shares retry policy and KV cache enablement steps, ava shares security and pricing docs.
[07:05] Olivia Chen: timeline?
[07:07] Ava Thompson: target next touchpoint after you've had the logs — let's aim for early next week 2026-05-11 for a deeper tuning session. i'll send invites.
[07:15] Samir Khan: quick note — we also have a security review coming up; ava, can you attach SOC2 and data residency info in the same packet?
[07:23] Ava Thompson: yes, will include SOC2 and KMS/HSM notes.
[07:26] Mira Patel: thanks. one more thing, diego, when you run the replay can you tag which runs produced 5xx vs timeouts vs 429s so we can correlate?
[07:35] Diego Rivera: absolutely. i'll include a CSV with labels.
[07:38] Olivia Chen: cool. anything else?
[07:40] Ava Thompson: no, that's it. thanks everyone. i'll follow up with a short email and share the drive folder.
[07:46] Samir Khan: thanks, bye.
